Tumor cell growth

In one breast-cancer cell study, red laser and blue LED did not change cell viability or migration but reduced invasion. The broader laboratory literature includes variable findings and does not show that PBM changes tumor growth in patients.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In one breast-cancer cell study, red laser and blue LED did not change cell viability or migration but reduced invasion. The broader laboratory literature includes variable findings and does not show that PBM changes tumor growth in patients.

Summary of the Evidence

The source category has 111 database records, representing 111 unique titles. Most are in-vitro or ex-vivo studies; three titles include mouse work, and one translational human-tagged record is not a controlled clinical tumor-growth study. Two narrative reviews and two systematic reviews summarize primary reports rather than add experiments. Method tags overlap within some titles.

Human and clinical evidence

No controlled clinical study directly tested whether PBM changes tumor growth in patients. The single human-tagged translational record includes laboratory or biomarker context and does not provide a patient-level tumor-growth comparison. It should not be interpreted as clinical evidence that PBM either promotes or suppresses cancer (da Silva et al. 2023).

Animal evidence

Three titles include mouse components. These in-vivo studies are distinct from cell-only experiments, but they are few relative to the large laboratory inventory and do not establish a general effect across tumor types or light protocols.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

The category includes 108 records tagged in-vitro or ex-vivo. In a breast-cancer-cell study, red laser and blue LED exposure did not change cell viability or migration, while invasion was reduced. Other titles study different cell lines, wavelengths, fluences, and timing, so results are not uniform. The example illustrates why a result from one cell model cannot be generalized to every tumor type (da Silva et al. 2023).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The laboratory inventory spans different light sources, wavelengths, power, fluence, exposure schedules, cell types, and experimental conditions. The database does not support one common dose range or an optimal tumor-cell protocol. Findings from isolated cells or mouse models do not reproduce whole-body light delivery, tumor microenvironments, or patient treatment decisions.

Interpretation

This category supports the statement that PBM effects on cancer cells are model- and protocol-dependent. It does not establish a clinical effect on tumor growth or progression in people.

Evidence strength in source summaryCancer-cell viability, migration, and invasion in laboratory models: Very low

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The category contains 111 unique titles, and most are laboratory studies with diverse cell types and protocols. One breast-cancer cell study found no change in viability or migration and lower invasion. Three records include animal components, and the human-tagged translational record does not establish tumor-growth effects in patients.
